title: Partial functors of a localized Quillen bifunctor are derived left adjoints
statement:
Use model categories and derived mapping-space adjunctions as in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], and homotopy coherent localizations and coherent functor categories as in [lem-coef-system-localization-universal]. Work in universes containing all the following categories. Let $\mathcal M,\mathcal N,\mathcal P$ be model categories with functorial factorizations, and write $\mathcal M^c,\mathcal N^c$ for their full subcategories of cofibrant objects. Write $q_{\mathcal M},q_{\mathcal N},q_{\mathcal P}$ for localization at their weak equivalences. Let $F:\mathcal M\times\mathcal N\to\mathcal P$ be an ordinary bifunctor such that $F(A,-)$ is a left Quillen functor for every cofibrant $A\in\mathcal M$ and $F(-,D)$ is a left Quillen functor for every cofibrant $D\in\mathcal N$. Left Quillen here means having an ordinary right adjoint and preserving cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Suppose a coherent bifunctor
$$B:\mathcal M_\infty\times\mathcal N_\infty\to\mathcal P_\infty$$
is equipped with a natural equivalence $B(q_{\mathcal M}A,q_{\mathcal N}D)\simeq q_{\mathcal P}F(A,D)$ on $N(\mathcal M^c\times\mathcal N^c)$, including its arrows and higher simplices. Then for every cofibrant $A$, there is an equivalence of coherent functors
$$B(q_{\mathcal M}A,-)\simeq\mathbf L(F(A,-)),$$
and for every cofibrant $D$, there is an equivalence $B(-,q_{\mathcal N}D)\simeq\mathbf L(F(-,D))$. These equivalences extend the specified comparison on cofibrant inputs using the canonical replacement weak equivalences. Each partial functor of $B$ at any object of either localized category has a right adjoint, with no simplicial enrichment or symmetry hypothesis.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Lemma 4.1.8.8 and its proof, printed pp. 493-494; Corollary 1.3.4.26 and Remark 1.3.4.27, printed pp. 119-120. Generic comparison underlying the ordered tensor application Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this coherent-localization assertion.

proof.text: Choose functorial cofibrant replacements $\epsilon_{\mathcal N}:Q_{\mathcal N}\to\mathrm{id}$ and $\epsilon_{\mathcal M}:Q_{\mathcal M}\to\mathrm{id}$ by factoring the initial maps as cofibrations followed by trivial fibrations. Naturality gives $\epsilon_{Y'}Q(f)=f\epsilon_Y$; for a weak equivalence $f$, two-out-of-three shows that $Q(f)$ is a weak equivalence between cofibrant objects. Fix a cofibrant $A\in\mathcal M$. By hypothesis $L_A=F(A,-)$ has an ordinary right adjoint $U_A$ and preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to this exact Quillen pair. It gives $T_A=\mathbf L L_A\dashv\mathbf R U_A$, with a coherent identification $T_Aq_{\mathcal N}\simeq H_A$, where $H_A(Y)=q_{\mathcal P}F(A,Q_{\mathcal N}Y)$. In particular $L_A$ preserves weak equivalences between cofibrant objects; together with the preceding calculation this shows that $H_A$ inverts every weak equivalence.

proof.text:
Write $G_A=B(q_{\mathcal M}A,-)$ and denote the specified comparison by $\gamma$. Precompose $\gamma$ with the ordinary functor $Y\mapsto(A,Q_{\mathcal N}Y)$ into $\mathcal M^c\times\mathcal N^c$. Since $q_{\mathcal N}(\epsilon_Y)$ is an equivalence, we obtain a natural equivalence of functors on $N(\mathcal N)$:
$$G_Aq_{\mathcal N}\xleftarrow{\ G_Aq_{\mathcal N}(\epsilon)\ }G_Aq_{\mathcal N}Q_{\mathcal N}\xrightarrow{\ \gamma_{A,Q_{\mathcal N}(-)}\ }H_A.$$
Both arrows are equivalences: the first because a functor preserves equivalences, the second by the assumed comparison on the whole nerve of the cofibrant-input category. Thus this is a coherent natural equivalence, including all simplices, rather than a collection of objectwise isomorphisms.

source.place: Lemma 4.1.8.8, printed pp. 493-494, and Remark 1.3.4.27, printed p. 120; agent-written general bifunctor comparison from the cited derived-adjunction and localization interfaces, rather than an application of the combinatorial hypothesis in Corollary 1.3.4.26.

proof.text: Both $G_Aq_{\mathcal N}$ and $T_Aq_{\mathcal N}$ invert weak equivalences. Apply [lem-coef-system-localization-universal] with $\mathcal C=N(\mathcal N)$, its system of weak equivalences, and $\mathcal E=\mathcal P_\infty$. Restriction along $q_{\mathcal N}$ is an equivalence onto the full functor subcategory inverting this system. Compose Step 2 with the inverse of the identification $T_Aq_{\mathcal N}\simeq H_A$ from Step 1. Full faithfulness of restriction lifts this equivalence to $\theta_A:G_A\simeq T_A$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal N_\infty,\mathcal P_\infty)$. Its inverse and the two inverse homotopies lift by the same full faithfulness, so the lifted transformation is an equivalence.

proof.text:
For a cofibrant $D\in\mathcal N$, both $Q_{\mathcal N}D$ and $D$ are cofibrant. Step 1 therefore implies that $q_{\mathcal P}F(A,\epsilon_D)$ is an equivalence. Use it as the canonical comparison $T_A(q_{\mathcal N}D)\simeq q_{\mathcal P}F(A,D)$. Naturality of the given $\gamma$ for the arrow $(1_A,\epsilon_D)$ in $\mathcal M^c\times\mathcal N^c$ gives
$$q_{\mathcal P}F(A,\epsilon_D)\,\gamma_{A,Q_{\mathcal N}D}\simeq\gamma_{A,D}\,G_A(q_{\mathcal N}\epsilon_D).$$
After inverting the rightmost equivalence, this says exactly that $\theta_A$ followed by the canonical derived comparison restricts to $\gamma_{A,D}$. This is an identity of natural transformations on $N(\mathcal N^c)$: it comes from precomposing the naturality of $\gamma$ with the natural transformation $Q_{\mathcal N}|_{\mathcal N^c}\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal N^c}$, hence includes all higher naturality simplices. It proves the required extension assertion.

source.place: Lemma 4.1.8.8, printed pp. 493-494, and Remark 1.3.4.27, printed p. 120; agent-written general bifunctor comparison from the cited derived-adjunction and localization interfaces, rather than an application of the combinatorial hypothesis in Corollary 1.3.4.26.

proof.text:
Fix instead a cofibrant $D\in\mathcal N$ and use the second Quillen pair $K_D=F(-,D)\dashv V_D$ from the hypotheses. By [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], $S_D=\mathbf L K_D\dashv\mathbf R V_D$ and $S_Dq_{\mathcal M}\simeq q_{\mathcal P}F(Q_{\mathcal M}(-),D)$. The comparison in this variable is the explicit natural zigzag
$$B(q_{\mathcal M}(-),q_{\mathcal N}D)\xleftarrow{\ B(q_{\mathcal M}\epsilon,q_{\mathcal N}D)\ }B(q_{\mathcal M}Q_{\mathcal M}(-),q_{\mathcal N}D)\xrightarrow{\ \gamma_{Q_{\mathcal M}(-),D}\ }q_{\mathcal P}F(Q_{\mathcal M}(-),D).$$
The two arrows are equivalences for exactly the two reasons given in Step 2. Apply [lem-coef-system-localization-universal] now to $N(\mathcal M)$ to lift this zigzag to $B(-,q_{\mathcal N}D)\simeq S_D$. On cofibrant $A$, naturality for $(\epsilon_A,1_D)$ gives $q_{\mathcal P}F(\epsilon_A,D)\gamma_{Q_{\mathcal M}A,D}\simeq\gamma_{A,D}B(q_{\mathcal M}\epsilon_A,q_{\mathcal N}D)$. Here $F(\epsilon_A,D)$ is a weak equivalence between cofibrant-input values by the cited Quillen result. Cancelling as in Step 4 proves the specified extension in this variable. No interchange of the two inputs of $F$ has been used.

source.place: Lemma 4.1.8.8, printed pp. 493-494, and Remark 1.3.4.27, printed p. 120; agent-written general bifunctor comparison from the cited derived-adjunction and localization interfaces, rather than an application of the combinatorial hypothesis in Corollary 1.3.4.26.

proof.text:
By [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], every $x\in\mathcal M_\infty$ is equivalent to $q_{\mathcal M}A$ for a cofibrant $A$. Choose $e:q_{\mathcal M}A\simeq x$. The bifunctor supplies a natural equivalence $B(e,-):G_A\simeq B(x,-)$. For $y\in\mathcal N_\infty$ and $z\in\mathcal P_\infty$, its inverse, Step 3, and Step 1 give the natural mapping-space equivalences
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P_\infty}(B(x,y),z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P_\infty}(T_A(y),z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal N_\infty}(y,\mathbf R U_A(z)).$$
Thus $\mathbf R U_A$ is a right adjoint to $B(x,-)$. Likewise the cited representative assertion in $\mathcal N$ writes any $d$ as an object equivalent to $q_{\mathcal N}D$ with $D$ cofibrant; the equivalence $B(-,q_{\mathcal N}D)\simeq B(-,d)$ and Step 5 give $\operatorname{Map}(B(x,d),z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(x,\mathbf R V_D(z))$. Hence every partial functor in the other variable also has a right adjoint. These equivalences are natural in the two mapping-space variables, so they assert actual infinity-categorical adjunctions. The argument used no enrichment or symmetry.
